title: Natural Domain and Graph of G(t) = 1 / |t|
originalTopic: Functions and Graphs: Domain and Graphing
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the natural domain and describe the graph of the function G(t) = 1 / |t|.
finalAnswer: \text{Domain: } (-\infty, 0) \cup (0, \infty); \quad \text{Even graph in Quadrants I and II with asymptotes } t = 0, y = 0

steps.title: Determine the Natural Domain
steps.explanation: Because the denominator |t| vanishes only at t = 0, the natural domain is the set of all non-zero real numbers.
steps.why: A rational expression is defined everywhere its denominator is non-zero.

steps.title: Write in Piecewise Form and Analyze Symmetry
steps.explanation: Since G(-t) = G(t), the function is even and symmetric about the vertical y-axis, taking strictly positive values for all t != 0.
steps.why: The absolute value in the denominator reflects the negative left branch of 1/t above the horizontal axis.

steps.title: Describe Asymptotic Behavior and Graph
steps.explanation: The graph consists of two symmetric hyperbolic branches in the first and second quadrants passing through (1, 1) and (-1, 1), rising toward +infinity along the vertical asymptote t = 0 and decaying toward the horizontal asymptote y = 0 as |t| -> infinity.
steps.why: As |t| approaches 0, its reciprocal 1/|t| grows without bound; as |t| grows without bound, 1/|t| approaches 0.
